items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: "I said, 'Joe Pask?' He said, 'Yeah, Joe Pask.' ... I still love Joe Pask."

ctx.x: he going to just lay out or going to get in your way, you know, when you're playing, one of those things.

I said, "Joe Pask?" He said, "Yeah, Joe Pask." But Joe plays the solos, one of these things, and that's it. And so I said, "Well, so and so, and I said, Well, okay, we'll leave it like that because I still love Joe Pask." So we got talking about Basie, and a funny thing came up. He said he walked up to Basie one day, and he said, "Basie, what you paying me all this bread for, man?" He said, "And I want to play something." He said, "Why don't you let me play?" Basie said, "What do you want to play?" He said,…

So this went into a lot of things -- it was a funny thing, and we laughed, and he says, "It's funny now. It wasn't funny then," he says. But he said, one time Basie cried on him. He said -- this was a funny little thing -- he said Basie wanted him to take a $100.00 cut. He was telling him how were bad hard times with band money, and these things, and he said, man, he was about to make him shed tears, he was telling him how bad things were, you know, and you felt sorry for Basie, you know. So he said, "Everything…
